technical_source_policy: primary/author/institution/arXiv sources; search snippets used only for discovery

sources.title: Translation Validation for Synchronous Languages
sources.finding: Per-translation automated validation is an established alternative to proving a translator correct globally. This directly collides with any claim that per-message translation validation itself is novel.

sources.title: TVOC: A Translation Validator for Optimizing Compilers
sources.authors: Barrett, Fang, Goldberg, Hu, Pnueli, Zuck
sources.finding: Checking source/target equivalence for each compiler run is established and automated with formal verification conditions. Generator-versus-validator separation is known prior art.

sources.title: The reduced product of abstract domains and the combination of decision procedures
sources.authors: Patrick Cousot, Radhia Cousot, Laurent Mauborgne
sources.finding: Independent abstract components can be combined by iterated pairwise reduction/exchange of observations. New components can be added by defining observation exchanges. This is a close mathematical collision with a lattice/intersection of partial semantic oracles.

sources.title: Towards a Complete Picture of Lens Laws
sources.finding: Forward/backward transformations linked by consistency laws are established. Round-trip consistency/lens-law framing is not novel.

sources.title: Synthesizing Symmetric Lenses
sources.finding: Symmetric lenses propagate information in both directions and explicitly handle information present on only one side. This collides with generic bidirectional-information claims.

sources.title: PICARD: Parsing Incrementally for Constrained Auto-Regressive Decoding from Language Models
sources.finding: Incremental parsing can reject inadmissible target-language tokens during generation. Grammar/formal-language validity is a strong conventional baseline but does not by itself establish source semantic fidelity.

sources.title: Structure-Invariant Testing for Machine Translation
sources.finding: Meaning-preserving source mutations plus output-structure relations are established as metamorphic MT testing. Metamorphic boundary adversaries are prior art, not candidate novelty.

sources.title: Word Closure-Based Metamorphic Testing for Machine Translation
sources.finding: Fine-grained source/output semantic relation comparison for MT error detection is established and improves violation-identification F1 over prior metamorphic comparators in that paper.

sources.title: Analysis of faults in an N-version software experiment
sources.finding: 27 independently prepared versions exhibited more coincident failures than expected under statistical independence; equivalent and different logical errors produced correlated failures. Independence of diverse translator/checker implementations must not be assumed.

collision_summary.surviving_candidate_scope: Project-specific composition only: tiny bounded German hard-field partial oracles + exact typed Clay hard projection + UNKNOWN-as-erasure + per-message admission witness + ExpressionState hard-field noninterference under Frank's codec-not-mind and ClayCode-only constraints.

strongest_external_countermechanism: A conventional independent semantic parser/validator, combined with constrained typed Clay output and explicit ambiguity handling, may achieve equal or stronger safety with less architecture. It must be the strongest benchmark baseline.
novelty_ceiling: NOVEL_COMBINATION_CANDIDATE at most unless later broader search and matched implementation evidence justify a stronger class
